## Welcome to Lab!

Lab meets **once a week, right after Monday lecture.** Think of it as the "hands-on" half of the course — lecture is where you learn the *why*, lab is where you practice the *how*.

::: highlight-last
-   Every lab pairs with recent lecture content

-   You'll work in R, using real (or realistic) data

-   Most labs end with a few questions to submit
:::

## How Lab Works

### Every Week, Roughly

1.  A short concept recap (2–3 minutes)

2.  A scenario and dataset to explore together

3.  Guided R code — you'll run it, tweak it, and predict what changes before you see the output

4.  A handful of short-answer questions, submitted on Brightspace before the following lab

## Submitting Your Work

::: highlight-last
-   Answers go on **Brightspace**, under that week's Lab assignment

-   Short answers are fine — I'm looking for *reasoning*, not essay length

-   Late work: see the syllabus for the policy; if something comes up, email me *before* the deadline
:::

## Setting Up Posit Cloud

We'll be using **Posit Cloud** (formerly RStudio Cloud) all semester — a browser-based version of RStudio, so there's nothing to install.

1.  Go to [posit.cloud](https://posit.cloud) and create a free account (use your FSC email)

2.  Join our class workspace using the link posted on Brightspace

3.  Open the "Lab Template" project — this is where you'll do your work each week

## A Few R Basics

::: highlight-last
-   R is **case-sensitive**: `Score` and `score` are different variables

-   `<-` assigns a value to a name: `x <- 5`

-   `|>` (the pipe) means "then do this next" — it chains steps together

-   If you get an error, read it. It usually tells you exactly what R didn't understand.
:::

## Icebreaker

### Everyday Statistics

Turn to a neighbor:

-   What's one number or statistic you've seen *this week* — in the news, on your phone, anywhere?

-   Do you trust it? Why or why not?

::: highlight-last
-   We'll come back to "should I trust this number?" all semester.
:::

## Icebreaker

### Your Relationship With Math

-   On a scale of 1 (dread) to 10 (bring it on), how do you feel about this class right now?

-   You are absolutely not alone if that number is low — statistics anxiety is extremely common, and it is not a measure of whether you'll do well here.

## Before Next Lab

::: highlight-last
-   Make sure your Posit Cloud account works and you can open the Lab Template project

-   Skim the syllabus, especially the lab and homework policies

-   Bring questions! There's no such thing as a bad one in this class.
:::
